text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SEVODNYA
- Most Russian tea importers are unhappy about an announced price rise of imported packed tea.
- Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin pledged to do everything necessary to fight terrorism.
- The government has decided to audit the biggest state-controlled companies such as Gazprom, Rosneft and others.
- International loans received by Russia go straight to social programs and do not help overcome the current economic current crisis.
- The new team of reformers in the Russian government wants to attract as many supporters as possible before forthcoming battles over budget and tax reforms.
- UNEXIM Bank, one of Russia's biggest banks, is planning to take part in an investment tender on a 51 percent stake of Sibneft shares.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko blames independent mass media and President Yeltsin's entourage for a drastic fall in public support for unification with Russia.
- Russia will have to make concessions in NATO talks to reach a special agreement to be signed in Paris on May 27.
- Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze accused Russia of supporting terrorists.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, appointed Fuel and Energy Minister, has joined a club of natural monopolies.
- Big Russian banks are likely to take part in an investment tender on Sibneft shares.
- Sberbank, Russia's state-controlled saving bank, is gradually becoming a main bank authorised to deal with the federal budget.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The Russian army, which was founded five years ago, is facing grave problems.
- NATO's eastward expansion is natural for Europe. It is also natural for Russia to be left out, an expert says.
- Natural monopolies will not be divided, but the state control over them should be restored, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said in an interview.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- The paper publishes the president's decree on the outlines of structural reform of natural monopolies.
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIA
- President Yeltsin's decrees on reforms of communal services and natural monopolies are aimed at robbing people of the last means that they have.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Boris Yeltsin is to sign on May 10 a decree on income and spendings declaration for state officers and members of their families. It is still not clear how this decree will be implemented.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
